newsitem.title: REUNION: Demonstrators occupy public building on Reunion.
newsitem.headline: Demonstrators occupy public building on Reunion.

text.p: Around one thousand demonstrators occupied a public building on the French Indian Ocean island of Reunion on Tuesday, vowing to stay overnight in a new protest against plans to cut officials' pay.
The demonstrators, mostly civil servants and students, overran the building which houses government offices and a courtroom in the centre of Saint-Denis. No injuries were reported.
The occupation followed clashes on Monday when several thousand protesters surrounded the island's international airport.

Last Thursday dozens of cars were set on fire, shops looted and 28 people arrested in a first outbreak of violence when groups of youths went on a rampage in the dilapidated Chaudron neighbourhood of the usually quiet tropical city, police said.

The main reason for the protests is resentment at government plans to start phasing out the extra 53 percent in salaries paid to civil servants stationed in France's overseas possessions, including those locally recruited.
Reunion, with a mixed population of 600,000 Creoles, Indians, Chinese and Europeans is broadly divided into two societies living side by side.
One is made up of people on the government payroll, ranging from top officials to sanitation workers, who have a European standard of living because of salaries higher than those in France.
The other lives in poverty because of widespread unemployment in the failing sugar cane industry.
